A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 17-page versions of Model Tinting, despite the changed title. The shared method, experiments, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original GLUE and vision model-merging results, a cross-task pilot study, and extensive ablations and analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds NYUv2 dense-prediction results, additional baseline evaluations, and an extended pilot study.

M1.justification: The documented algorithm retains joint optimization of merging coefficients and task-specific layers, individual-model supervision, and the same relative-confidence filtering rule. Internal-layer adaptation and sequential updates already appear in v1; their reframing and relocation do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds NYUv2 indoor scenes with semantic segmentation, depth estimation, and surface-normal estimation. These introduce substantially different task requirements beyond the retained eight GLUE tasks and 8-, 14-, and 20-task image-classification evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 adds LiNeS to the NLP comparison and TA with LiNeS to retained vision comparisons, including Appendix Tables A–B. Traditional MTL and MagMax newly enter the NLP comparison in Table 3, although both were already evaluated on vision tasks in v1. The existing comparator suite is otherwise retained.

E3.justification: The new dense-prediction evaluation uses ResNet-50, segmentation/depth/angular-error metrics, and 400 samples per task over 25 iterations, with batch size 16 and learning rate 0.0001. The pilot also adds an AdaMerging encoder condition alongside Task Arithmetic. Retained main classification and NLP settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The pilot adds analysis of how Task Arithmetic versus AdaMerging features affect classifier transfer. Conversely, v1's fixed-coefficient layer ablation in Figure 4 and Table C(a) is removed. The joint layer-and-coefficient ablation already existed in v1's Figure C/Table C(b) and is retained, alongside the other loss, initialization, convergence, and sparsity analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests for its experiments. The existing Spearman-correlation analyses retain the same statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds NYUv2 results, including segmentation mIoU of 49.0/50.2 for Tinting/Tinting++, additional baseline scores, and AdaMerging pilot outcomes; fixed-coefficient layer results are removed. Retained benchmark scores are unchanged, including Tinting's GLUE average of 0.8404 and ViT-B/32 Tinting/Tinting++ averages of 89.6/90.1. These changes primarily expand the reported evidence rather than improve same-setting performance.

T1.justification: Task-vector definitions, merging equations, the supervised pilot objective, and the joint optimization objective remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs; v2's additional explanations do not introduce new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The central single-layer adaptation, joint optimization, and confidence-filtering contributions remain. v2 explicitly extends its headline performance claim to dense prediction and quantifies the lightweight-adaptation claim as requiring as little as 0.5% of parameters.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the extended pilot as showing that shared-encoder choice can limit cross-task transfer even after classifier training. It also discusses heterogeneous dense-prediction tasks and contrasts Surgery's depth/normal weaknesses with EMR-Merging's segmentation weakness. Existing interpretations concerning entropy, sparsity, initialization, and excessive layer adaptation largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the dense-prediction backbone, initialization, learning rate, sample budget, iterations, and batch size, and adds a 0.5M-versus-7M trainable-parameter comparison. Existing code access and classification/NLP training details remain; the sequential-update discussion moves to Appendix B.1.

R1.justification: The introduction and Section 2.2 substantially revise positioning from a critique of shared representations toward avoiding extra modules while adapting the shared encoder. New discussions include weight alignment and latent task-specific knowledge, citing works such as Git Re-Basin, ZipIt!, Localize-and-Stitch, and LiNeS. Table 1 formalizes the revised comparison with prior approaches.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, pilot narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 adds explicit contribution bullets, moves implementation discussion into the appendix, brings prediction-discrepancy analysis into Section 4.2, and reorganizes the empirical narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds method-comparison and dense-prediction tables, redraws and relocates the radar charts, and replaces the main pilot heatmaps with summary bars while expanding the heatmaps in the appendix. It promotes the existing joint-training layer plot, removes the fixed-coefficient display, and substantially rearranges appendix tables and sparsity figures.

improvement.justification: NYUv2 evaluation, broader baseline comparisons, and the added shared-encoder control strengthen validation and motivation beyond v1's already extensive experiments. Clearer positioning and organization also help assessment. These gains outweigh the loss of the fixed-coefficient layer ablation, although dense-prediction loss and filtering details remain limited.
